qt: to the Commission Dolors Montserrat (PPE), Javier Zarzalejos (PPE) Subject:

In 2020, the European Parliament called for all necessary measures to be taken to prevent victims of terrorism being humiliated by acts such as tributes to ETA members. The report, which was adopted by the European Parliament’s Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs, contained amendments aimed at putting an end to tributes to ETA members and the psychological damage that these acts inflict on victims. The relevant institutions, whether at local, regional or state level, were asked to provide the necessary safeguards to prevent further victimisation resulting from humiliation and attacks on the victims’ image. It has recently been revealed that, in 2023, more than 450 public events supporting the terrorist group ETA took place in Spain. In light of this: 1.
Is the Commission showing support for the victims of ETA and calling on the institutions to take steps to prevent acts of support or remembrance for terrorists and the criminal gang itself?
Does it reject any kind of act or show of support for ETA prisoners who took lives and sought to spread terror to destroy freedom?

(14 March 2024) The Commission has shown its continued support for victims of terrorism, their associations and has also encouraged their involvement in preventing radicalisation. The Victims’ Rights Directive (1) provides for a set of binding rights for victims of all crimes, including victims of terrorism. In addition, the directive on combating terrorism (2) responds more directly to the specific needs of victims of terrorism. The Commission has set up the EU Centre of Expertise for Victims of Terrorism (3) to promote integrated support for victims of terrorism in all EU Member States. In the EU Strategy on victims’ rights (2020 — 2025) (4), the Commission highlights the need to ensure specialist support to protect victims of terrorism. The Commission Victims’ Rights’ Coordinator ensures a smooth coordination of EU level actions for victims of terrorism within the EU Victims’ Rights Platform. Furthermore, the Commission supports the Radicalisation Awareness Network ‘Practitioners’ (RAN), an umbrella network connecting practitioners involved in preventing radicalisation and violent extremism throughout Europe. The RAN has a specific Working Group dedicated to support victims of terrorism, which maintains a network of victims’ organisations and contributes every year on 11 March to the organisation of the European Remembrance Day of Victims of Terrorism. Finally, the 2023 Communication on a comprehensive approach to mental health (5) contains 20 flagship initiatives that promote good mental health and addresses the prevention and treatment of mental health problems, including for victims of crime.
